title: ‘Everyone Is Depleted’
gist: Yemen has fallen back into full civil war, with a September Houthi offensive securing effective control over the Bab el-Mandeb and more than 800 deaths since early August. Aid groups warn of worsening hunger in a country importing ~90% of its food, as shipping disruptions from the Iran war and Black Sea push global food prices up while U.S. funding cuts leave Yemen's response only 20% funded.

themes.theme: Renewed civil war and Red Sea control

insights.claim: Yemen's 2022 truce has unraveled; in early September the Iran-backed Houthis launched an offensive that made major gains along the Red Sea coast and secured effective control over the Bab el-Mandeb.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Houthi control of the Bab el-Mandeb raises risk to Red Sea/Suez shipping on top of Hormuz disruptions, pressuring freight, insurance and energy prices.
insights.quote: securing effective control over the Bab el-Mandeb
insights.locator: A devastating civil war broke out

insights.claim: The WHO reports more than 800 deaths in Yemen since early August, with casualties rising at roughly 100 per day between Sept. 19 and 26, and over 145,000 people displaced since June according to the IOM.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Rapid escalation suggests the conflict will not quickly stabilize.

insights.claim: WFP acting chief Carl Skau said the Houthis are ignoring humanitarian immunities, detaining 38 WFP staff in Sanaa and occupying WFP offices in Mokha, making operations very difficult.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Aid access constraints raise the likelihood of famine-level outcomes.

themes.theme: Shipping disruptions and global food prices

insights.claim: Skau says shipping disruptions from the Iran war in the Strait of Hormuz and the Russia-Ukraine war in the Black Sea are already adding pressure to world food prices, and WFP anticipates tens of millions more people will be pushed into acute hunger.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Chokepoint disruptions are feeding global food inflation, a risk for food-importing emerging markets.
insights.quote: we are anticipating that tens of millions of people will be pushed into acute hunger because of that.

insights.claim: Yemen imports around 90 percent of its food; more than 18 million people face acute food insecurity and 2.2 million children under five face acute malnutrition, per WFP.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Import dependence makes Yemen highly exposed to maritime and price shocks.

insights.claim: Yemen is one of three countries where the U.S. has cut all its humanitarian funding, and only 20 percent of Yemen's humanitarian response needs are funded.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: U.S. aid retrenchment leaves a gap other donors (e.g., Gulf states) may need to fill.
